Which ion drifts? Charge transfer vs Penning

Ar/iC₄H₁₀ 95/5 · MX17 Micromegas · 2026-10-15

Two different processes both end with an isobutane ion. They are easy to mix up because both happen for the same reason: argon's energy levels sit above isobutane's ionization energy. They change different parts of the signal.

Ion charge transfer

Ar⁺ + iC₄H₁₀ → Ar + iC₄H₁₀⁺

An ion passes its charge to an isobutane molecule within about 1 ns. This decides which ion drifts, so it sets the ion mobility and the speed of the ion tail.

Penning transfer

Ar* + iC₄H₁₀ → Ar + iC₄H₁₀⁺ + e⁻

An excited neutral argon atom ionizes isobutane and frees an extra electron. This raises the gain and changes the α(E) slope (EnablePenningTransfer, rP).

1 · The energy ladder

2 · Charge transfer: which ion drifts

Ions drift left toward the mesh. Watch the speed trace underneath. Each Ar⁺–Ar collision moves the charge onto an argon atom at rest, so the Ar⁺ trace keeps dropping back to zero. After the hop onto isobutane, the hydrocarbon ion has no partner it can hand its charge to, so collisions only slow it down and its average speed is higher.

3 · Penning: an extra electron

An avalanche electron excites an argon atom instead of ionizing it. In pure argon that energy leaves as a UV photon. With isobutane present, a collision with the Ar* uses the energy to ionize an isobutane molecule, which adds one more free electron to the avalanche.

4 · Why it matters: the ion tail

Same avalanche, same 128 µm gap at 490 V, two mobilities. The ions start near the strips, because the avalanche grows exponentially toward the anode. They then drift up to the mesh, and the induced current lasts as long as the slowest ones are still moving. Both curves carry the same total charge; the hydrocarbon ion delivers it about 2.4 times sooner.

Why do Garfield++ and Magboltz reduce Penning transfer to one fitted number, and drift every ion as Ar⁺? The main obstacle is missing data, not computing power and not unsolvable physics. The heavy-particle rates are mostly unmeasured, gain curves can't separate them, and the quantum mechanics that could compute them has never been attempted for Ar* + isobutane.

Data

Branching ratios are unmeasured

The fraction of Ar* quenching collisions that ionize the quencher has been measured for one pair only: Ar metastables + C₂H₂ (0.61–0.74). Every other value is an estimate.

Degeneracy

A gain curve measures one sum

Gain only fixes Σ ri·νexc,i, so many different per-level fractions reproduce the same curve. Fitting more gain data doesn't break that tie.

Theory

Ab initio stops at diatomics

Penning ionization has been computed only for He*/Ne* + Ar, H₂ and HD. Ar* + C₄H₁₀ would need a many-dimensional ionization-width surface, and nobody has tried.

1 · One number standing in for many unknowns

Each group of Ar levels has its own Penning fraction ri. The width of each bar is that group's share of excitations; its fill is ri. As the fractions change, the total shaded area stays fixed, and so does the gain curve. That is why Şahin et al. fit one r (and could not separate 4p from 3d), and why Schindler's 15-parameter de-excitation model could only be tuned to r, not used to predict it.

2 · What has actually been measured

These are the inputs a first-principles Penning model would need for Ar/iC₄H₁₀. Electron-side inputs are in good shape. The heavy-particle side, which is what Penning transfer actually is, is mostly empty.

Garfield++'s de-excitation source still labels two of its constants "order of magnitude guess" and "seems high, to be checked!". Isobutane's VUV photo-absorption and ionization yield are also missing.

3 · What Garfield does with rP

In microscopic tracking, Garfield's "simplified Penning" creates the extra electron instantly, at the point of excitation (λ = 0 by default). In a real gas the Ar* lives for a collision time first (about 2 ns at 5 % iso), and some of the energy travels 10–100 µm as a VUV photon. The mean gain comes out the same by construction, because rP is fitted to it. Timing, avalanche width and gain fluctuations do not. A 128 µm gap, where the whole avalanche lasts about 1 ns, is where the approximation is least safe.

4 · Who can simulate what

mature
Electron transport. Magboltz, BOLSIG+, LoKI-B/MC, ThunderBoltz. Plasma solvers add superelastic collisions and excited-state populations that Garfield++ lacks.
mature tools
Plasma chemistry. ZDPlasKin, LoKI-B+C, QDB, ThunderBoltz handle Ar metastable kinetics, Penning ionization and radiation trapping routinely. An Ar/iso reaction set could be written in a day; its branching ratios could not.
solved
e⁻ + Ar excitation, using B-spline R-matrix theory (Zatsarinny & Bartschat).
barely
e⁻ + isobutane. The only ab initio calculation found is elastic scattering, 10–50 eV, from 2004.
benchmark only
Ab initio Penning ionization. He*/Ne* + Ar, H₂, HD with complex optical potentials, checked against millikelvin merged-beam experiments (Narevicius). The authors still call the potential surfaces a major obstacle.
never attempted
Ar* + iC₄H₁₀ (or CO₂). No calculation found.
blind to it
Machine-learning inverse swarm (Stokes, White, Brunger). It fits electron cross sections; Penning is heavy-particle chemistry that electron swarm data cannot see.
plasma codes only
Ion species and reactions. Garfield++ allows one mobility table per gas, with no charge transfer or clustering. At 1 atm that's fine, because conversion takes about 1 ns and condensation microseconds, as long as it is the right species.

5 · The ion-tail budget

The drifting ion is t-C₄H₉⁺-like. Coimbra measured K₀ ≈ 2.26 in 98/2 Ar/iso and 2.16 ± 0.02 in Ar/CF₄/iso 95/3/2, both close to the Langevin limit. Nothing has been measured above about 45 Td, so K₀ ≈ 2.05 at gap fields is an extrapolation. Switch the field to see why the field map decides the story.
